title: 4,500 Google Employees Demand Job Security as Alphabet Hits $4.3 Trillion Valuation
excerpt: The Alphabet Workers Union delivered a petition to CEO Sundar Pichai seeking guaranteed severance, voluntary buyouts, and an end to forced performance curves — demands that resonate with visa-holding Indian tech workers.
body:
• Over 4,500 Google employees have signed a petition delivered to CEO Sundar Pichai demanding guaranteed severance, voluntary buyouts before layoffs, and an end to forced performance quotas.
  • Alphabet has laid off more than 14,000 people since early 2023, even as the company reported $109.9 billion in quarterly revenue and a $4.3 trillion market cap.
  • The Alphabet Workers Union wants laid-off employees, especially those on work visas, to receive severance as extended paid leave rather than a lump sum to allow time to find new employment.
  • The campaign reflects a broader shift across Big Tech, where companies are cutting jobs while pouring billions into AI, leaving workers anxious about long-term job security.

About 100 Google employees gathered outside Alphabet's Mountain View headquarters on July 17, holding signs reading "Googlers for Job Security" and chanting slogans directed at management. They delivered a petition bearing more than 4,500 signatures to the office of CEO Sundar Pichai — what union leaders called the largest piece of employee feedback Google has ever received about job security.

What the Workers Are Demanding

The petition, organised by the Alphabet Workers Union (AWU), lays out four core demands. Workers want guaranteed severance at least equal to the terms offered during the January 2023 mass layoffs — 16 weeks of base pay plus additional weeks per year of service. They want voluntary buyouts offered before any involuntary layoffs. They want laid-off employees to have the option of taking severance as extended paid leave rather than a lump sum. And they want an end to what they describe as a quota-based performance rating system that forces managers to fit evaluations to a curve rather than reflect actual performance.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=vto4emrvuiY

"Make no mistake: this is a company that is enjoying massive, unprecedented success."

— Parul Koul, Google software engineer and Alphabet Workers Union president

The paid leave option carries particular urgency for employees on H-1B and other work visas. When visa-holding workers lose their jobs, they typically have only 60 days to find a new employer or face the prospect of leaving the country. Extended paid leave would give them more time to secure new positions without disrupting their immigration status.

Record Profits, Ongoing Cuts

The petition comes against a backdrop of extraordinary financial performance. Alphabet's latest quarter produced $109.9 billion in revenue, up 22% year-over-year, while operating income climbed 30% to $39.7 billion. The company is now the third-largest in the world by market capitalisation, valued at approximately $4.3 trillion.

Yet Alphabet has laid off more than 14,000 people since early 2023. The largest single round, in January 2023, cut roughly 12,000 roles. Smaller rounds have continued since — Google Cloud saw layoffs approximately two months ago, and CNBC reported last year that the company eliminated more than a third of managers overseeing small teams.

"These layoffs and cuts are not difficult decisions, but simply profit being put over the people that make this company run," Koul told reporters outside headquarters after delivering the petition.

A Wider Industry Anxiety

Google's situation mirrors a pattern across Big Tech. Since 2022, companies including Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft have collectively cut tens of thousands of jobs through repeated rounds. The layoffs have often coincided with massive increases in AI spending, creating a dissonance that has left workers across the sector uncertain about their long-term prospects.

The AWU itself has around 1,400 dues-paying members among Alphabet's roughly 191,000 employees. The union has historically focused on issues like ethics, diversity, and contractor treatment. The pivot to job security marks a shift toward bread-and-butter labor concerns.

The Indian Diaspora Connection

The protests resonate particularly with Indian-origin tech workers, who make up a significant portion of Google's engineering workforce and are disproportionately affected by visa-linked job insecurity. The petition's demand for extended paid leave as an alternative to lump-sum severance directly addresses the precarious situation of H-1B workers who face tight timelines to find new sponsorship after a layoff.

Google has not publicly responded to the petition's specific demands. A staff member in Pichai's office accepted the document and agreed to pass it on to the CEO. Whether the company engages with the demands or treats them as background noise will likely depend on whether the campaign gains broader traction within the 191,000-person workforce.
